blocks.text: Lima Cathedral and its twin towers beside a spacious square, Peru
Lima: the cathedral, palm trees and street lamps on the city square
Lima: colonial centre, Casa Aliaga and the Gold Museum

After breakfast, your sightseeing tour of Lima begins at 09:00 and includes a visit to Casa Aliaga. The mansion was built in May 1536, around the time of the city’s founding, on the foundations of an older building. It belonged to the Spanish conquistador Jerónimo de Aliaga, an associate of Francisco Pizarro, and remained connected to the same family for generations. Inside, surviving furnishings and interiors give you a sense of how wealthy residents of colonial Lima lived.

The Spanish founded Lima in 1535, and the city also became known as the City of Kings. In the colonial era, cathedrals, mansions and the viceroy’s palace were built here. The tour takes you through Miraflores, with its Park of Love, then through San Isidro, home to El Olivar Park and old estates. Along the way, you’ll get a panoramic view of Huaca Pucllana, an ancient pyramid thought to date back about 2,500 years.

Huaca Pucllana offers a different view of Lima’s history. This large archaeological complex survives within the modern city. The contrast is especially clear after passing through Miraflores and San Isidro, with their modern buildings, parks, restaurants and busy streets.

In the historic centre, see the Plaza de Armas, City Hall, the Government Palace and the cathedral, where Francisco Pizarro is buried. Another major stop is the Gold Museum, which houses a large private collection of gold and silver jewellery, objects made with precious stones, textiles and ceramics. Return to your hotel after the tour.
